title: Meerkats Task Trace v1 — input/output + trajectory
description: One user request, end to end. Captures the raw input, the router classification, the validated task instance, the trajectory as a flat span list (tree via parent_span_id, OTel-shaped), and the outcome. Stage artifacts (resolved_selection, execution_plan, query results, diagnosis_result) are stored by reference and cited from spans, so the trace stays small and every referenced artifact remains independently schema-valid. Because resolver artifacts carry data_as_of + catalog_version, a trace is replayable, not just observable.

artifact_ref.description: Pointer to a stored artifact (or a small inline payload). conforms_to names the schema $id it validates against, so the trace is self-describing.

conforms_to.description: schema $id the artifact validates against, e.g. …/query_and_act/v1.json#/$defs/query_task

ref.description: content address / URI of the stored artifact (immutable; content-addressed enables replay)

inline.description: small payloads embedded directly instead of by ref

digest.description: hash of the artifact bytes, for integrity + dedupe

classification.description: Router output — the otherwise-dark NL → intent step.

alternatives.description: runner-up intents the router considered, for auditing misclassification

span.description: One stage of the trajectory. Tree is reconstructed from parent_span_id (null at root). Maps directly to an OTel span.

stage.description: subquery = a query an agentic intent fired internally (its output is an evidence artifact)

attributes.description: open OTel-style key/values, e.g. { evidence_id, member_count, risk_level }

status.description: terminal state, e.g. ok / error / awaiting_approval / data_quality_blocked

output.description: the final result artifact (query rows, execution result, diagnosis_result, …)

data_as_of.description: data snapshot the result was computed against — the replay anchor

input.description: raw request as received — the input side of input/output tracing

actor_ref.description: server-side principal reference; never PII in the trace

task.description: the validated task instance the LLM produced — must itself pass the router
